selected_variables: route geometry validity at the distal span

decision.hypothesis: Key physical problem: the present design must produce at least 10 mm local material displacement while holding tip displacement below 5 mm and settling by the frozen tail window, but the installed tendon path is already reported to intersect segment_2_cell_4 at time zero. Competing H1: sparse/illegal distal routing and associated loss or misdirection of unilateral constraint authority causes the large distal tip transfer; a geometry-valid redistributed route is therefore prerequisite. Competing H2: the route report is incidental to the simulated transfer and the remaining failures are mainly finite-time damping/relaxation, so increasing or redistributing viscosity would fix qualification while preserving response. A third plausible alternative is insufficient distal structural stiffness, requiring stiffness redistribution rather than more damping. Existing evidence discriminates only partly: matched viscosity changes improve drift and some velocity measures but do not reliably resolve speed or static-balance qualification, while s7_positive has 82.95 mm point motion but 72.29 mm tip motion (ratio 0.871), strongly weakening a damping-only account; however no legal-route matched comparison exists, so routing versus stiffness remains unresolved. Next route: use the existing mechanism-research interface to diagnose route validity and unilateral constraint state first, then design a geometry-valid distal guide/anchor redistribution before any further full-task or acceptance run; do not change the frozen task and do not infer acceptance from this diagnosis.
decision.expected_observation: If H1 is correct, route diagnostics will reproduce the distal cable-solid intersection and show that the current installed path cannot supply a geometry-valid constraint transfer; a later legal redistribution should sharply reduce s7 tip/point ratio while retaining point displacement. If H2 is correct, routing will prove legal or irrelevant and matched damping changes will monotonically reduce tip speed, monitor speed, qvel and static-balance residual without materially degrading point, tip and ratio margins. If stiffness redistribution is primary, route validity will be recoverable but distal transfer will remain excessive unless distal tangent stiffness is increased relative to the loaded region.
decision.weakening_observation: H1 is weakened if a complete checked route is legal and a matched geometry-valid routing change leaves distal tip transfer unchanged. H2 is refuted by the observed non-monotonic/static-balance response to viscosity and would be further weakened if additional legal damping cannot meet all four loaded qualification limits. The stiffness alternative is weakened if a legal routing correction alone reduces the distal ratio below 0.3 with acceptable response and settling.
decision.fixed_conditions: Keep the frozen ten-condition task, gravity, mount, force programs, 0.000125 s timestep, solver settings, qualification windows and thresholds unchanged. Hold segment count, total 0.28 m flexible length, mesh, masses, 3 mm circular sections, 2 MPa modulus, four tendons and no active control fixed during the immediate diagnosis. Treat sampled native dynamics, hard-equilibrium mathematics, route validity and independent acceptance as separate evidence layers; do not use untested conditions as evidence.
decision.stopping_condition: Stop this diagnostic branch when route legality and the loaded active/slack constraint state are determined for the current candidate. Do not expand to all ten conditions or independent acceptance until a geometry-valid candidate passes the selected development cases' response bounds and loaded qualification checks.
decision.interpretation: The recorded evidence supports prioritizing a prerequisite physical uncertainty—whether the tendon route is physically valid and actually supplies distal restraint—over further scalar damping tuning. Current local mathematics and sampled finite dynamics do not establish full-task success, and the explicit illegal-route record prevents treating favorable s3 displacement values as an admissible design result.

decision.selected_method: mechanism_research: paired guide-routing effect on finite-time passive response

decision.hypothesis: Key physical problem: obtain at least 10 mm local x-displacement under every ±0.1 N load while keeping tip motion, lateral motion, and loaded settling within qualification, using a physically legal unilateral tendon route. H1: sparse/tapered distal guiding causes cable-solid intersection and poor or unstable load transfer; correcting distal guide placement/clearance will preserve or improve local response while reducing loaded residual motion. H2: routing is not the performance-limiting mechanism; the dominant problem is insufficient dissipation or structural stiffness, so legalizing the route alone will not cure loaded speed/static-balance failures and may reduce desired local compliance. Existing evidence discriminates only partly: it directly establishes illegal installed geometry for the studied F3 route, while viscosity variants still failed loaded qualification, but no matched legal-route comparison exists, so the causal performance hypothesis remains unresolved.
decision.expected_observation: In a subsequent matched finite-time mechanism study, a minimally rerouted, clearance-valid distal guide variant has no cable-solid intersection over the sampled route, retains local projected displacement at or above 0.01 m with tip displacement at or below 0.005 m and ratio at or below 0.3, and lowers loaded tip/monitor speed and static-balance residual relative to the unchanged baseline. That pattern supports H1 and justifies full ten-load qualification before independent replay.
decision.weakening_observation: A legal matched reroute leaves loaded speed/static-balance residual unchanged or worse, or materially reduces local displacement below 0.01 m / violates the ratio or tip bounds while the baseline response persists; this weakens H1 and shifts the next design variable to damping/stiffness. Any remaining route intersection refutes the proposed geometry repair itself.
decision.fixed_conditions: Keep the frozen task, gravity, mount, ten load programs, ±0.1 N forces, timing, timestep, evaluator bounds, no-contact rule, initialization and hard-equilibrium procedure unchanged. Hold segment count, lengths, materials, cross-sections, payout lengths, tendon count, force limits, and all non-distal routing parameters fixed; compare only a minimal distal guide-position/clearance edit against the same baseline. Treat sampled native dynamics as diagnostic, geometry validity separately, and reserve full independent acceptance for a later complete replay.
decision.stopping_condition: Do not proceed to acceptance until a candidate is route-legal and a complete frozen ten-load evaluation passes every response and qualification bound. Stop this mechanism branch after a matched legal-route comparison clearly fails to improve qualification without sacrificing response, then investigate damping/stiffness instead.
decision.interpretation: The next uncertainty to resolve is whether the illegal distal tendon path is merely a validity defect or also the mechanism behind the response-versus-settling tradeoff. A matched routing study is higher priority than more viscosity tuning because current evidence already shows loaded qualification failures across viscosity variants, whereas geometry is conclusively illegal and has never been repaired under matched conditions.

The paired routing proposal directly tests whether legalizing the route improves qualification without sacrificing response, while preserving uncertainty about the cause. It needs a more explicit geometry-preflight and fixed-payout interpretation. Coverage is 3/5 groups.
